canonical_statement: The review aims to summarize the prevalence, risk factors, clinical features, proposed mechanisms, and management strategies for aromatase inhibitor-associated musculoskeletal syndrome (AIMSS).

The review characterizes AIMSS primarily as aromatase inhibitor-associated bone loss and aromatase inhibitor-induced arthralgia, with musculoskeletal symptoms that can impair quality of life and treatment adherence.
The review reports a meta-analysis of 21 studies (13,177 participants) in which aromatase-inhibitor-associated arthralgia prevalence ranged from 20% to 74%, with a pooled estimate of 46%.

population.label: Participants in 21 studies summarized by the cited meta-analysis

quantitative_result.original_result_text: prevalence ... ranging from 20-74% with a pooled estimate of 46%

canonical_statement: The review reports that breast cancer recurrence occurred in 20% of patients who discontinued endocrine therapy versus 11% of women who completed recommended treatment.

population.label: Breast cancer patients in a cited adherence study

canonical_statement: The review reports that nearly one quarter of women receiving aromatase inhibitors for risk reduction discontinued therapy because of AIMSS at a median of 6 months.

population.label: Women receiving aromatase inhibitors for risk reduction in early-stage breast cancer

quantitative_result.original_result_text: nearly a quarter ... discontinue therapy at a median time of 6 months due to AIMSS

canonical_statement: Among patients who switched to a second aromatase inhibitor because of adverse effects, the review reports that 38% tolerated the second agent for a median of 13 months.

population.label: Patients switching to a second aromatase inhibitor because of adverse effects

canonical_statement: The review concludes that reported AIMSS risk factors are inconsistent across studies; obesity, recent menopause, prior hormone replacement therapy, and taxane exposure have been implicated but not uniformly replicated.
The review reports retrospective ATAC and IES analyses associating BMI greater than 30 kg/m² and weight greater than 80 kg, respectively, with increased AIMSS risk.

population.label: Participants in retrospective analyses of ATAC and IES

quantitative_result.original_result_text: BMI >30 and weight >80 kg ... correlated with increased risk for AIMSS

canonical_statement: The review reports that prior taxane chemotherapy was associated with an estimated fourfold risk of AI-associated joint pain and stiffness in one cross-sectional survey, while noting that this association was not consistently replicated.

population.label: Women receiving aromatase inhibitors in a cited cross-sectional survey

quantitative_result.original_result_text: estimated to have four times the risk

canonical_statement: A meta-analysis of 13 phase III trials summarized by the review reported arthralgia rates of 1-47% with AI monotherapy versus 5.8-33.3% with combined AI plus CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy.

population.label: Participants in 13 phase III trials summarized by a cited meta-analysis

quantitative_result.effect_measure: reported arthralgia range in AI monotherapy
quantitative_result.original_result_text: arthralgias in 1-47% ... AI monotherapy compared to 5.8-33.3% ... combined treatment

canonical_statement: The review states that lower musculoskeletal symptom ranges were also observed in AI plus CDK4/6 inhibitor groups for myalgia, back pain, and bone pain, but larger trials were considered necessary before attributing a protective effect.

The review reports a meta-analysis of seven randomized trials (30,023 patients) in which longer aromatase inhibitor duration was associated with increased fracture odds (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.34-1.61; p<0.001).

population.label: Patients in seven randomized controlled trials

canonical_statement: The review reports that anastrozole, letrozole, and exemestane lower serum estrogen levels by approximately 81-94%, 88-98%, and 52-72%, respectively, in postmenopausal women.

population.label: Postmenopausal women summarized by cited pharmacology studies

quantitative_result.effect_measure: reported estrogen suppression range for anastrozole

canonical_statement: The review proposes estrogen deprivation as a central mechanism of AI-induced bone loss through increased pro-resorptive signaling, including RANKL and inflammatory cytokines, together with loss of osteoprotegerin-mediated restraint of osteoclastogenesis.
The review reports a case-cohort GWAS of 1,071 AI-treated patients that identified three SNPs in or near six genes associated with increased fracture risk.

population.label: AI-treated patients in cited case-cohort GWAS

quantitative_result.effect_measure: sample size with reported fracture-associated SNP signal
quantitative_result.original_result_text: GWAS using samples from 1071 patients identified three SNPs in or near six genes

canonical_statement: The review presents a proposed AIA definition requiring all four major criteria plus at least three of six minor criteria.

Major proposed AIA criteria are current AI therapy, new or worsened joint pain after AI initiation, improvement or resolution within 2 weeks of stopping the AI, and recurrence of pain after restarting the AI.

Minor proposed AIA criteria include symmetrical joint pain, hand or wrist pain, carpal tunnel syndrome, decreased grip strength, morning stiffness, and improvement in joint discomfort with use or exercise.

AIA is described as symmetrical pain and stiffness commonly affecting the hands, wrists, knees, ankles, and shoulders, with possible axial involvement, decreased grip strength, myalgias, carpal tunnel syndrome, and trigger finger.
The review reports a median AIA onset of approximately 6 weeks after starting an aromatase inhibitor, with peak symptoms around 6 months.

population.label: Patients developing aromatase-inhibitor-induced arthralgia

quantitative_result.original_result_text: median time to onset is approximately 6 weeks with peak symptoms at 6 months

canonical_statement: The review reports that 20-30% of patients discontinue aromatase inhibitor treatment early because of intolerance and that 75% of these discontinuations cite arthralgia as the primary reason.

population.label: Patients intolerant of aromatase inhibitor therapy

arms.arm_label: Discontinuations citing arthralgia as primary reason

quantitative_result.original_result_text: 20-30% ... discontinue treatment early, with 75% ... citing arthralgias as the primary reason

canonical_statement: The review reports an ESR1 variant (rs9322336) associated with musculoskeletal-toxicity-related exemestane discontinuation (HR 5.0, 95% CI 2.1-11.8; p<0.0002).

population.label: Participants in a cited randomized clinical trial

canonical_statement: The review reports that HSD17B2 SNP rs11648233 was associated with increased odds of AIA (OR 2.21, 95% CI 1.55-3.16) in a study of 1,049 women receiving aromatase inhibitors.

population.label: Women receiving aromatase inhibitors in cited genetic study

canonical_statement: The review reports that musculoskeletal sonography in AI-treated patients found increased tendon thickness (p<0.001) and more joint effusions (p<0.033).

population.label: AI-treated patients in a cited musculoskeletal sonography study

quantitative_result.effect_measure: p-value threshold for increased tendon thickness
quantitative_result.original_result_text: increased tendon thickness (p<0.001) and higher rates of joint effusions (p<0.033)

canonical_statement: The review discusses estrogen deprivation, pro-inflammatory cytokine signaling, altered nociception, tenosynovial inflammation, autoimmune activation, and genetic susceptibility as plausible mechanisms for AIA, but treats these mechanisms as incompletely established.
A single-blind crossover trial summarized by the review found joint pain in 3% of participants during letrozole treatment versus 11% during anastrozole treatment (p=0.025).

population.label: Women with HR+ breast cancer in a cited single-blind crossover trial

quantitative_result.effect_measure: joint pain percentage in letrozole arm

canonical_statement: In the ATOLL study summarized by the review, 71.5% of 179 patients who switched from anastrozole to letrozole remained on letrozole at 6 months and 28.5% discontinued because of persistent AIMSS.

population.label: Patients discontinuing anastrozole because of AIMSS and switching to letrozole

canonical_statement: The review reports that ATOLL participants who remained on letrozole still had high rates of arthralgia (73.9%), myalgia (21%), arthritis (15.9%), tendinitis (14%), and polyalgic syndrome (12.7%).

population.label: ATOLL participants remaining on letrozole after switching

canonical_statement: The MA.27 trial summary reports osteoporosis in 31% of exemestane-treated patients versus 35% of anastrozole-treated patients (p=0.001), while a further MA.27 analysis found no significant BMD difference at 24 months.

population.label: Participants in MA.27

canonical_statement: The review states that no head-to-head study had been designed to compare all three third-generation aromatase inhibitors specifically for AIMSS manifestations and severity.

For short-term AIMSS pain control, the review states that NSAIDs and acetaminophen can be used and that opioids should not be used; it also concludes that no single mitigation strategy has proven uniformly effective.
A phase II trial summarized in Table 2 reports pain reduction at 3 months in 43% of patients receiving testosterone 40 mg and 70% receiving testosterone 80 mg, with the 80 mg group reaching p=0.04.

population.label: Women receiving adjuvant anastrozole in a cited phase II testosterone trial

quantitative_result.effect_measure: pain reduction percentage in 80 mg testosterone group

canonical_statement: The subsequent A221102 trial summarized by the review reports that roughly two thirds of participants improved at 3 months, but there was no significant difference between topical testosterone and placebo.

population.label: Postmenopausal women with moderate-to-severe arthralgia on adjuvant AI

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Two thirds of patients reported improvement ... although there was no significant difference between the two groups

canonical_statement: In a randomized trial of approximately 300 AIMSS patients, duloxetine produced a clinically significant (>2-point) joint-pain reduction at week 6 in 68% versus 49% with placebo (p=0.003).

population.label: Patients with AIMSS in a cited randomized duloxetine trial

exposures.details: 30 mg week 1, 60 mg weeks 2-11, then 30 mg week 12

canonical_statement: The same duloxetine trial summary reports an average joint-pain score 0.82 points lower with duloxetine at 12 weeks, but adverse events in 78% versus 50% with placebo and convergence of pain scores after discontinuation.

population.label: Patients with AIMSS in cited randomized duloxetine trial

canonical_statement: SWOG S1202 is summarized as showing patient-reported treatment benefit in 73.3% with duloxetine versus 41.8% with placebo; the 95% CI for the between-group difference was 15.4 to 47.2 percentage points.

population.label: Patients in SWOG S1202

quantitative_result.original_result_text: 73.3% vs 41.8%; 95% CI for difference = 15.4-47.2 percentage points

canonical_statement: A SWOG S1202 subgroup analysis summarized by the review found a greater pain reduction in obese patients receiving duloxetine than placebo (-2.73 vs -1.64 points; p=0.003), whereas non-obese patients had similar reductions (-2.46 vs -2.34; p=0.75).

population.label: Obese patients (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) in SWOG S1202

quantitative_result.effect_measure: pain-score change in duloxetine obese subgroup

canonical_statement: The SOLE trial summary reports better musculoskeletal-pain-related quality-of-life scores with intermittent versus continuous letrozole (mean score change 3; 95% CI 0-6; p=0.023), without improvement in disease-free survival.

population.label: Postmenopausal women in SOLE after 4-6 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy

exposures.details: 9 months on/3 months off in years 1-4; daily in year 5

canonical_statement: In an observational cohort of 36,472 breast cancer patients summarized by the review, high-fracture-risk AI users treated with bisphosphonates had HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.51-1.04) for fractures compared with those not receiving bisphosphonates.

population.label: Breast cancer patients in cited observational cohort

canonical_statement: The same cohort summary reports a subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.69 (95% CI 0.48-0.98) for fracture with bisphosphonate treatment among high-risk AI users.

population.label: High-fracture-risk AI users in cited observational cohort

canonical_statement: The review reports that ABCSG-18 participants receiving denosumab for 3 years had fewer fractures and significantly higher femoral-neck and lumbar-spine BMD than placebo-treated participants.

population.label: AI-treated participants in ABCSG-18

concept.text: Fracture incidence and bone mineral density

canonical_statement: The single-arm ZAP trial summary reports AIA in 37% of patients receiving zoledronic acid with letrozole versus 67% in historical ELPh controls (p<0.001).

population.label: Postmenopausal breast cancer patients in ZAP

exposures.details: before AI and again at 6 months

canonical_statement: A retrospective analysis summarized by the review reports musculoskeletal symptoms in 6.97% of chronic diuretic users versus 15.85% of nonusers during adjuvant AI therapy (p=0.01).

population.label: Women receiving adjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy

canonical_statement: A phase II diuretic trial summarized by the review reports improved lower-limb WOMAC scores after 4 weeks, including total WOMAC 17 versus 29 (p<0.001), stiffness 2.3 versus 3.9 (p=0.002), and function 8.7 versus 15 (p<0.001).

population.label: Women with AIMSS in cited phase II diuretic trial

concept.text: Furosemide 20 mg plus spironolactone 50 mg daily

quantitative_result.effect_measure: total WOMAC score in diuretic group

canonical_statement: A 27-patient single-arm study summarized by the review reports improvement in AIMSS pain in 67% after one week of prednisolone, with approximately half still reporting benefit at 2 months.

population.label: Patients with AIMSS in cited prednisolone study

canonical_statement: A prospective vitamin D cohort summarized by the review found that joint pain increased overall by a mean 1.16 VAS points (SD 2.66; p<0.001), but the increase was smaller among patients who achieved 25(OH)D concentrations at least 40 ng/mL (p=0.02).

population.label: Breast cancer patients receiving vitamin D during AI therapy

exposures.details: additional 16,000 IU every 2 weeks for baseline 25(OH)D <30 ng/mL

quantitative_result.original_result_text: mean 1.16 points SD 2.66; P < 0.001; increase significantly less ... ≥40 ng/ml, p=0.02

canonical_statement: Another vitamin D cohort summarized by the review reports a lower proportion with disability among those achieving 25(OH)D above 66 ng/mL versus those at or below 66 ng/mL (19% vs 52%; p=0.026).

population.label: Letrozole-treated patients receiving vitamin D3

concept.text: Vitamin D3 supplementation with achieved 25(OH)D >66 ng/mL

canonical_statement: A randomized trial summarized by the review found no significant difference in AIMSS score change between vitamin D3 600 IU and 4,000 IU daily for 6 months (p=0.38).

population.label: Breast cancer patients with AIMSS in cited vitamin D3 trial

canonical_statement: The review summarizes a 60-patient vitamin D2 randomized trial as showing lower pain scores at 2 months (p=0.02) but no significant difference at 6 months.

population.label: Patients in cited vitamin D2 randomized trial

canonical_statement: The review summarizes a 93-patient vitamin D3 trial terminated after no difference at 12 weeks between high-dose and standard-dose regimens (54% vs 57%).

population.label: Patients in cited high-dose versus standard-dose vitamin D3 trial

quantitative_result.effect_measure: reported response percentage in high-dose arm

canonical_statement: A prospective glucosamine/chondroitin study summarized in Table 2 reports improvement in pain scores in 46.2% of 53 participants after 24 weeks.

population.label: Participants in cited glucosamine/chondroitin study

exposures.details: glucosamine 1500 mg + chondroitin 1200 mg daily for 24 weeks

canonical_statement: Table 2 summarizes the main omega-3 randomized trial as showing no statistically significant between-group difference in pain scores at 12 or 24 weeks despite improvement over time.

population.label: Participants in cited omega-3 randomized trial

quantitative_result.original_result_text: no statistical difference in pain scores based on BPI, WOMAC, and M-SACRAH

canonical_statement: In the prose discussion of SWOG S0927, the review states that BPI-SF symptoms decreased by mean 2.22 points with omega-3 versus 1.81 with placebo (p<0.001), creating an apparent tension with Table 2, which says there was no significant between-group difference.

population.label: Women in SWOG S0927

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean symptom decrease in omega-3 group

canonical_statement: A meta-analysis of nine exercise studies (743 participants) summarized by the review found improvements in pain (p=0.006), stiffness (p=0.01), and grip strength (p=0.002), with interventions lasting 6 weeks to 12 months and at least 120 minutes of exercise per week.

population.label: Participants in nine exercise studies

exposures.details: aerobic exercise with or without resistance exercise; at least 120 minutes/week

canonical_statement: A 95-patient study summarized by the review reports that 90% of participants assigned to 4 weeks of yoga reported reduced symptom severity.

population.label: Breast cancer patients on AI or tamoxifen in cited yoga study

canonical_statement: In a 226-patient acupuncture RCT summarized by the review, BPI worst-pain decreased by 2 points with true acupuncture versus 1 point with sham acupuncture and 1 point with no treatment after 6 weeks.

population.label: Patients in cited acupuncture randomized controlled trial

quantitative_result.effect_measure: pain-score decrease in true acupuncture group

canonical_statement: The same acupuncture trial summary reports at least a 2-point improvement in 58% with true acupuncture, 33% with sham acupuncture, and 31% with no treatment.

population.label: Patients in cited acupuncture randomized controlled trial

quantitative_result.effect_measure: response percentage in true acupuncture group

canonical_statement: The review identifies active research on bone microarchitecture, cartilage biomarkers, genetic risk signatures, and management strategies including auriculotherapy, physical therapy, curcumin, cannabidiol, and tai chi.
The review concludes that deeper understanding of AIMSS mechanisms is needed to identify patients at risk and develop more effective, tolerable preventive and therapeutic strategies.
The authors declare that the research was conducted in the absence of commercial or financial relationships that could be construed as a potential conflict of interest.
